5-1142 DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Colville Indian Agency, Nespelem, Wash., Feb. 6, 1920 Mr. C. V. Peel, Officer in Charge, Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. Dear Mr. Peel; Please advise me the condition of Harry McDonald. His father says that the boy is sick and should be permitted to return home. I told him that I would not make recommendation without ascertaining the facts from you. Very truly yours, [signature] Superintendent. RS:AJ Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., Feb. 9, 1920 Mr. Fred C. Morgan, Supt. Colville Indian Agency Nespelem, Washington Dear Mr. Morgan: Replying to your letter of February 6, 1920, you are advised that at the present time Harry McDonald is confined in the school hospital with Measles, but is getting along nicely, the school nurse informs me. Aside from having the measles, Harry has been enjoying good health and it is not thought necessary to send him home on account of ill health. Very respectfully, Special Agent in Charge. :MG RECORD OF PUPIL IN SCHOOL CUSHMAN AGENCY School. TACOMA, WASHINGTON (Location.) Supt. E. H. Hammond, Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Washington. Dear Mr. Hammond: The father of Charles and Harry McDonald has requested that I send you funds from the bank accounts of these two boys, so that they can return during the vacation period. I find that a check for $25.00 was sent to you May 27th from funds to the credit of Charles and that a check for $10.00 was sent to Harry May 9th. The following checks are enclosed at that time: ck No. 3050 for $10.00, payable to your order, against the account of Charles McDonald, ck No. 3051 for $25.00, payable to your order, against the account of Harry McDonald. An application, signed by the father, for the return of these two pupils is enclosed, which I recommend be given favorable consideration. Very truly yours, Fred C. Morgan Superintendent. SJ-Encls. ENTRANCE DATE March 3 DISEASE Broncho Pneumonia SYMPTOMS Pain in right side over back Temperature 105 3/4° at 5 P.M. High all night. Vomited at first. TREATMENT Laxative Then enema Some relief Still very sick. REMARKS Restless until 2:30 A.M. slept a little while Was a weak boy so still too weak to walk, but is a great deal better. Eat well & light died Still in hospital but doing fine Returned Dormitory April 17 - 1919 PHYSICIAN'S CERTIFICATE I hereby certify that I have this day carefully examined the above-named child herein proposed for transfer and find him to be in proper physical condition to attend school, and not afflicted with tuberculosis or any disease which would be a menace to the health of other pupils. Each boy should devote five weeks to the work of this department during the three prevocational years. When he has accomplished the work as outlined in the course of study in a satisfactory manner, a suitable rating should be recorded. Ratings must be based on a practical application as well as a knowledge of the principles involved. Ratings should be excellent (E), good (G), fair (F). If pupil's work is not worthy of a rating of fair, no grade should be recorded. Under "Remarks" mention anything that indicates interest, conduct, and proficiency of the pupil. This card should be filed in folder for record of pupil (5-197). When the pupil is transferred to another school a copy of this card should be sent to the officer in charge of the school to which he is transferred.
